title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 41
paragraphs: Thus did Xerxes march out of Sardis, and he would change, whenever it suited him, from his chariot to a traveling carriage. Behind him went a thousand spearmen — the best and most noble of the Persians — holding their spears in the usual manner. After them came another thousand cavalry picked from the Persians; and after those horsemen, ten thousand men selected from the rest of the Persians. These went on foot, and of them a thousand had golden pomegranates on their spears instead of butt-spikes, and these enclosed the remaining nine thousand on all sides, who had silver pomegranates. Those who had their spear-points turned toward the earth also had golden pomegranates; those who followed immediately after Xerxes had golden apples. Behind the ten thousand was stationed a force of ten thousand Persian cavalry; and after the cavalry there was a gap of some two stades. Then the rest of the army came on, marching all mixed together.
